status_summary: The Office of China Coordination is listed in State's Foreign Affairs Manual, was led by China Coordinator Joshua Young until 2026-10-02 and has since been overseen by Robert J. Palladino, a Deputy Assistant Secretary in the Bureau of East Asian and Pacific Affairs whom State's pages do not title China Coordinator. State's biography page for Palladino, read on state.gov on 2026-10-28, lists him in that post from 2026-10-02, overseeing the Office of China Coordination and the Office of Taiwan Coordination, after service as Senior Bureau Official for the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs from 2025-12-01 until 2026-08-17. The manual's chapter on the Bureau of East Asian and Pacific Affairs (1 FAM 130, last revised 2025-03-25, reconfirmed on fam.state.gov on 2026-10-26) lists the office at section 1 FAM 134, headed by a China Coordinator who also serves as a Deputy Assistant Secretary in the bureau, with three Deputy China Coordinators, reporting to the bureau's Assistant Secretary, through the bureau to the Under Secretary for Political Affairs and also to the Deputy Secretary; it names no person, that section's text is dated 2023-10-23, and the chapter still lists the Office of Multilateral Affairs that NPR reported closed in July 2025, so it may not reflect later changes. State's biography page for Joshua Young, read on 2026-10-26, states that he served as the State Department China Coordinator and Deputy Assistant Secretary in the same bureau, overseeing the same two offices, and lists him as Senior Bureau Official for the Bureau of Emerging Threats from 2026-10-02; it gives no dates for the coordinator service. World Journal reported on 2025-07-25, citing officials, that Young would take over the office as its fourth coordinator since 2022 and would report directly to the Under Secretary for Political Affairs rather than through the bureau's Assistant Secretary; Taiwan News reported the same appointment on 2025-07-31, citing Nikkei Asia, without stating a reporting line, and Taipei Times reported it on 2025-08-01. A Paraguayan government news agency report of 2026-05-05 identified Young as the State Department's Coordinator for China and a Deputy Assistant Secretary in that bureau, consistent with the manual's placement rather than the direct reporting line one 2025 report described. A House bill introduced on 2025-09-11 (H.R. 5329) describes the office as an existing part of the East Asia bureau. NPR reported on 2025-07-24 that the July 2025 reduction in force closed a different East Asia office, the Office of Multilateral Affairs, which covered ASEAN and South China Sea issues, with State saying mission-critical functions would be integrated elsewhere. The bureau's leadership page on state.gov, read on 2026-10-26 (page metadata then showed a last modification on 2026-10-20) and re-read on 2026-10-28, lists the same nine officials on both dates, none titled China Coordinator; Palladino appears as a Deputy Assistant Secretary without a portfolio. A Federal Register query on 2026-10-18 returned no document naming the office since 2025-01-20, and no State document found says the office was closed. The office is therefore rated operative in substance under a named official, at the implemented floor with match partial, because State does not confirm the coordinator title, staffing or current reporting line and the Mandate's concerns about staff assigned from other bureaus and interagency coordination are not shown to be addressed.

timeline.event: NPR reported that the July 2025 reduction in force closed State's Office of Multilateral Affairs in the East Asia bureau, which covered ASEAN and South China Sea issues; State said mission-critical functions would be integrated elsewhere.

World Journal reported, citing officials, that Joshua Young would lead the Office of China Coordination and report directly to the Under Secretary for Political Affairs, with the office remaining in the East Asia bureau.

Taiwan News, citing Nikkei Asia, reported that Joshua Young was appointed head of the Office of China Coordination and deputy assistant secretary for China and Taiwan, quoting an unnamed State official that the department was looking to elevate its focus on China; it does not state a reporting line.

H.R. 5329, the Regional China Officer Authorization Act, was introduced and referred to the House Foreign Affairs Committee; it would establish a unit inside the Office of China Coordination in the East Asia bureau.

Paraguay's state news agency reports a Washington meeting between the Paraguayan foreign minister and Joshua Young, identified as the State Department's Coordinator for China and a Deputy Assistant Secretary in the Bureau of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, which places the office and its head in the East Asia bureau as of May 2026.

State's biography page for Joshua Young lists him as Senior Bureau Official for the Bureau of Emerging Threats from October 2, 2026, and states that he previously served as the State Department China Coordinator and Deputy Assistant Secretary in the Bureau of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, where he oversaw the Office of China Coordination and the Office of Taiwan Coordination; the page gives no dates for that earlier service and names no successor.

Robert J. Palladino began serving as Deputy Assistant Secretary in the Bureau of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, overseeing the Office of China Coordination and the Office of Taiwan Coordination, according to his State Department biography (October 2, 2026 to present); he had served as Senior Bureau Official for the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs from 2025-12-01 to 2026-08-17, and the biography does not use the title China Coordinator.

title: Support and keep a centralized China policy office at State (China House)
uncertainties: The 2025 appointment rests on three news reports: World Journal (Chinese-language, citing unnamed officials), Taiwan News (citing Nikkei Asia and an unnamed State official) and Taipei Times (reporting department confirmation on 2025-07-31); only World Journal states the direct reporting line to the Under Secretary. State's Foreign Affairs Manual (fam.state.gov, reconfirmed on 2026-10-26) lists the office at 1 FAM 134 with the coordinator role, three Deputy China Coordinators and the reporting line, and names no person; that section is dated 2023-10-23 and the chapter 2025-03-25, and the chapter still lists the Office of Multilateral Affairs that NPR reported closed in July 2025, so the manual lags the reorganization. Twenty-four searches on 2026-10-26 returned no 2025 or 2026 state.gov announcement naming a China Coordinator, and a state.gov spokesperson archive page returned an error page; Young's biography page was then opened directly on 2026-10-26. That biography confirms the appointment and the office's existence through 2026-10-02 and the change of holder on that date, but gives no start date for the coordinator service, so the 2025-07-25 appointment date still rests on the news reports. Robert J. Palladino's biography on state.gov, read on 2026-10-28, shows him as Deputy Assistant Secretary from 2026-10-02 overseeing the Office of China Coordination and the Office of Taiwan Coordination, the portfolio Young held, but neither it nor the bureau's leadership page (re-read on 2026-10-28, listing the same nine officials as on 2026-10-26, with Palladino as Deputy Assistant Secretary and no portfolio; when read on 2026-10-26 the page showed no visible date and its metadata a last modification on 2026-10-20) uses the title China Coordinator, and no state.gov page found says whether that title lapsed, is held but not printed, or rests with someone else. A House payroll report notification for the week of 2025-07-28 titled Appointment of Joshua Young as China Coordinator appeared in search results and was not opened. A Federal Register API query for the office's name since 2025-01-20 returned 0 documents. The Agencia IP page of 2026-05-05 (ip.gov.py, the Paraguayan state news agency), opened on 2026-10-26, identifies Joshua Young as Coordinator for China at the State Department and a deputy assistant secretary in the Bureau of East Asian and Pacific Affairs; it does not name the Office of China Coordination as such or state a reporting line, so the direct reporting line to the Under Secretary described by World Journal in 2025 is unconfirmed, and it predates the 2026-10-02 change of holder. A National Review commentary of 2025-04-29 said the April 2025 reorganization offered no China-specific reforms. Inference: the Mandate asks that the concept be supported with adjustments; with the office listed in the manual and the portfolio Young held overseen by a named Deputy Assistant Secretary from 2026-10-02, the office is rated operative in substance, at the floor of the implemented band with match partial, but three limits remain: State's pages do not give Palladino the China Coordinator title that 1 FAM 134 assigns to the office's head, the manual section describing the office dates from 2023-10-23 and lags the 2025 reorganization, and the direct reporting line to the Under Secretary described in 2025 is unconfirmed; the staffing and interagency concerns the text raises are not shown to be addressed.
